articles.headline: Lillard: Blazers' crowded backcourt 'will work itself out'
articles.description: Damian Lillard said he's not worried about balancing a backcourt that includes himself, Ja Morant, Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson, saying it "will work itself out."
articles.headlineJa: リラード：ブレイザーズの混雑したバックコートは「自然と解決するだろう」
articles.descriptionJa: デイミアン・リラードは、自身、ジャ・モラント、ジュルー・ホリデー、スクート・ヘンダーソンを擁するバックコートのバランスを取ることについて心配しておらず、「自然と解決する」と語った。
articles.body:
PORTLAND -- Damian Lillard asked to be traded from the Portland Trail Blazers in summer 2023 because he didn't feel the team had a realistic chance to contend and needed to rebuild. The team did just that while he was away for two seasons with the Milwaukee Bucks and out last season recovering from a ruptured Achilles tendon.

Now that he's back on the court for the Blazers, the question is how new coach Micah Nori will make the surplus of backcourt talent fit together.

"If we are just doing the right thing, playing the right way ... I think the balance will work itself out," Lillard said, when asked how the team will deploy newly-acquired, former All Star guard Ja Morant, former lottery pick Scoot Henderson and two-time NBA champion Jrue Holiday.

"If our mentality is right and we handle it right, I think we could be a tough time for everybody," Lillard added. "If I get the ball and I'm advancing the ball ahead to Ja Morant, I feel pretty good about it. If I'm advancing the ball to [All Star forward] Deni [Avdija] out there, I feel good about it. And for both of those guys, if they are attacking the rim, attacking the paint and they're kicking the ball out to me for a 3-pointer, I think they should feel great about that."

Lillard, 35, missed all of last season recovering from a torn Achilles that he suffered in his final game with the Milwaukee Bucks. The only public glimpse of him in a Blazers uniform came at the All-Star game in Los Angeles when he won the 3-point contest. He's been spotted in workout videos looking very much like his old self on the court. Monday he said that he's been fully recovered from his injury for several months and only thinks about it when he's asked.

"I don't have any restrictions," he said. "I talk about the injury when I'm asked about it, but when I'm playing, it's not a thought anymore. I'm at that stage. I'm able to play free."

 

Nori, who was hired after a protracted and controversial coaching search led by a mandate by new owner Tom Dundon to control costs, said that he and Lillard have spent a lot of early mornings in the Trail Blazers facility talking about the team and the potential it has.

"Dame literally just wants to win, I think that's the only thing left he really has to do," Nori said. "As far as physically, I've seen him in the gym and the individual workouts. ...He's in as good a shape as he's been in, like he's told me, in his whole career."

As far as balancing the guard-heavy roster, Nori and general manager Joe Cronin suggested that Holiday could see some time on the wing -- noting he defended San Antonio center Victor Wembanyama during last season's first-round playoff series. Nori also noted that an abundance of ballhandlers -- which also includes Avdija, who was put into more of a point forward role by former head coach Tiago Splitter last year -- will help take some of the load off of Lillard.

The NBA season is right around the corner as media days concluded on Monday.

The Houston Rockets and Dallas Mavericks were the first two teams to hold media days last week, as they'll travel to China for a preseason doubleheader. The remaining teams went on Monday with plenty of storylines ahead of a new campaign.

LeBron James and Jaylen Brown headlined the new look Philadelphia 76ers. The New York Knicks rang in the season as champions for the first time in over 50 years. New York's opponents in the NBA Finals, the San Antonio Spurs, eye a return to the final stage, while the Oklahoma City Thunder prepared for revenge after losing to San Antonio in the Western Conference finals.

Here are the top scenes from 2026 NBA media day.

Atlanta Hawks

The offseason acquisition of Lu Dort creates a strong group of defenders in Atlanta with Nickeil Alexander-Walker and Dyson Daniels, who posed together.

Boston Celtics

The blockbuster trade that sent Jaylen Brown to the 76ers created a new Celtics duo: Jayson Tatum and Paul George. The two posed together, while Tatum praised his latest teammate.

Brooklyn Nets

If Brooklyn is in need of any bodies, head coach Jordi Fernandez may be the likeliest to come off the bench. 

Charlotte Hornets

A key offseason acquisition, Naz Reid looked right at home in the Hornets uniform.

Energy was high as players arrived for media day, pinpointing what they were looking forward to the most on the day. Two of the Bulls' young stars -- Matas Buzelis and 2026 No. 4 pick Caleb Wilson -- discussed celebrations. 

Cleveland Cavaliers

Cleveland displayed its new look core after acquiring wing Peyton Watson in a scene full of laughs.

Denver Nuggets

For the third straight year, a joker card showed up for Nikola Jokic with this one the biggest yet. Also, various Denver players took turns handling the Nuggets' X page, posting throughout the day.

articles.headline: J.J. McCarthy traded to Giants: Will he succeed in New York?
articles.description: With Jaxson Dart out for the season, the Giants dealt a fifth-round pick to Minnesota for McCarthy. But does this move the needle for New York? Can it work?
articles.headlineJa: J.J.マッカーシーがジャイアンツへトレード：彼はニューヨークで成功できるか？
articles.descriptionJa: ジャクソン・ダートが今季絶望となったため、ジャイアンツはドラフト5巡目指名権と引き換えにミネソタからマッカーシーを獲得した。しかし、この獲得はニューヨークの状況を変えるのだろうか？うまく機能するのか？
articles.body:
After Jaxson Dart went down with a season-ending knee injury in Week 2, it was probably inevitable that the Giants would add another quarterback to their roster. Jameis Winston can be combustible at his best, and while the weather wasn't great at MetLife Stadium on Sunday, he has averaged 4.7 yards per attempt and completed 51% of his passes since inheriting the starting job. With Jake Haener as the only other QB on the roster, getting someone to back up Winston and potentially take over if he continues to struggle was a no-brainer for the Giants.

And while Giants fans might have loved the idea of adding someone like Joe Flacco to continue the veteran's tour of Northeast football, teams weren't about to trade a useful backup who was one injury away from being their starter to the Giants out of pity. The market was QB3s, not QB2s, which left one very clear choice for New York: J.J. McCarthy

Landing a fifth-round pick for McCarthy was an obvious call for the Vikings. Once their quarterback of the future after they traded up to take him in the first round of the 2024 draft, McCarthy had quickly and brutally fallen out of favor in Minnesota. After being the NFC Offensive Player of the Week in his NFL debut last season -- an opening-week win over the Bears -- McCarthy's inability to work all areas of the field, operate within the structure of the offense or avoid negative plays frustrated a Vikings organization that had let Sam Darnold leave in free agency to hand the job to him.

Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show'

While it was no surprise when McCarthy lost something resembling a QB competition to new starter Kyler Murray in training camp this summer, the writing was really on the wall once it became clear that Kevin O'Connell preferred Carson Wentz as his second option. Trading McCarthy netted some small amount of draft capital for the Vikings while also saving them $4.6 million over the next two years in the process.

So, the trade makes sense for both organizations. Will it work out for McCarthy, who is still only 23 years old and younger than Ty Simpson, whom the Rams took with their first-round pick in this year's draft? We're living in a bit of a golden era of second (or third) acts for quarterbacks around the NFL, with the likes of Darnold, Bryce Young, Malik Willis, Baker Mayfield and others enjoying varying levels of success after their first organization gave up (and/or benched) them before the end of their rookie deals. Could McCarthy be the next to follow in their footsteps and turn his career around after a rough start?

In the wake of the Giants' trade, I'll argue both sides of that question. I'm not sure where I'll land, but I can see a case for McCarthy thriving in New York, and I can see one where he disappoints Giants fans who are hoping for an answer. articles.headline: Warriors' Steph Curry on choosing to extend: 'This is home'
articles.description: Stephen Curry called Golden State "home" in his first public appearance since signing a two-year, $116 million extension with the Warriors.
articles.headlineJa: ウォリアーズのステフィン・カリー、契約延長を選んだ理由：「ここが自分のホーム」
articles.descriptionJa: ステフィン・カリーは、ウォリアーズと2年1億1600万ドルの契約延長にサインして以来初の公の場で、ゴールデンステートを「ホーム」と呼んだ。
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO -- In his first public appearance since signing a two-year, $116 million extension with the Golden State Warriors, superstar point guard Stephen Curry explained why he decided to recommit to the only NBA franchise he has ever known.

"This is home," Curry said. "This is what we've built. This is a community that I've played in front of my entire career. Being able to finish the story the right way is a big part of what I can control."

Curry entered the offseason on a one-year, $62.6 million expiring contract. He became eligible for an extension on Aug. 29 and general manager Mike Dunleavy immediately gave Curry a menu of options, including a contract up to his max or a wait-and-see approach, which would've delivered the front office extra time and financial flexibility.

Curry contemplated for nearly a month and landed on the two-year, $116 million middle ground approach this past Friday, giving him late-career security and the Warriors some extra financial breathing room.

It's more than $20 million below the two-year, $136.7 million Curry was eligible to sign, but it includes a player option in the second season, so Curry has only truly committed to a $10 million pay cut for a single season.

"We're all smart people in this room," Curry said. "So you can kind of read the tea leaves on why it's designed the way that it is."

Dunleavy and the Warriors' front office have intentionally loaded their books with large expiring contracts, setting themselves up for an ocean of cap space to either be leveraged near the trade deadline or utilized next summer.

Curry's $55.7 million contract for 2027-28 cuts that theoretical cap space nearly in half, but the $10 million pay cut is enough of a gift to give the Warriors some extra cushion in their planning.

"I'm not fast-forwarding to February," Curry said. "I'm not fast-forwarding to next offseason. None of that. It's start Game 1, try to win. If we're competitive and doing what we're supposed to do, then that's information learned on how we need to get better."

The already wounded Warriors were delivered an extra bit of bad news Monday. Starting center Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely with another "health issue," as Dunleavy termed it, after missing large chunks of the past two seasons with a mysterious illness.

Porzingis will not travel with the team to Hawai'i on Monday night, ruling him out for the first four practices of training camp and the preseason opener next Sunday against the LA Clippers in Honolulu.

"I'm not marking him down as being out to start the [regular] season or anything like that," Dunleavy said. "He's just not available this week."

The Warriors are already without starting wings Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody, both limited to individual light court work in the middle stages of rehab for significant knee injuries. They won't be back in the lineup for multiple months.

The other 28 teams in the association joined them Monday, ahead of training camps beginning for most teams.

How will LeBron James and Jaylen Brown look in their new Philadelphia 76ers uniforms? What will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first media day away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their first impressions?

Sept. 28

SGA on chance at historic third straight MVP

At Oklahoma City Thunder media day, guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander discussed the possibility of winning a third straight NBA MVP award and if that's something he ponders going into this season.

"No different than any other year: Try to be the best player I can be, try to implement the things I just worked on," Gilgeous-Alexander said.

"The decision for MVP is literally 82 games away. I'm not going to win the award in the first week of the season. ... That kind of recipe for me in the past has kind of worked, and I've been fortunate to win two in a row. ...

We need to be laser focused on ourselves. We need to take the lessons from that [Western Conference finals] series for sure, and we did. But it's certainly not something that we overcorrect for because you end up chasing your shadow, and it prevents you from being your best as you move forward."

ESPN's Summer Forecast gave Gilgeous-Alexander the fourth-best chance at the 2027 MVP, behind Victor Wembanyama, Nikola Jokic and Luka Doncic. No player has won three consecutive MVPs since Larry Bird in 1984, 1985 and 1986. -- Baxter Holmes

Doncic talks LeBron exit, Lakers "championship" ceiling

Speaking to ESPN's Brian Windhorst during Los Angeles Lakers media day, guard Luka Doncic detailed his reaction to LeBron James leaving for the Philadelphia 76ers this past summer and why he thinks a successful 2026-27 includes a Lakers run to the title.

"It was kind of sad. Playing with LeBron was amazing. There's a lot of things I learned from him. ... We all know who LeBron James is."

Simmons 'didn't touch a ball for a year'

"The expectations are low. I feel like that's been something on me too, so we can relate in that way," Simmons told reporters. "I think we have a chip on our shoulder."

articles.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy football.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Sept. 28: Jets, Saints grapple with RB injuries

By Michael F. Florio

New York Jets RB Breece Hall is week-to-week after suffering a quad injury on Sunday, per Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter. Rapoport reported that the injury is not as significant as feared.

That leaves Braelon Allen and Isaiah Davis active for the Jets. I would anticipate that Allen, who has been the RB2 behind Hall for the last three years, starts and handles the majority of ground work. Both backs have handled limited volume in their careers, but Allen has been the superior runner of the two. He has a 51% success rate.

Davis is a bit of an explosive runner and has been effective as a pass catcher out of the backfield. While he does not have a touch this season, he has caught 75% of the targets that has gone his way and averaged 8.7 yards per catch.

Both Jets backs are worth adding in fantasy as this plays itself out in the coming weeks. Allen will be a flex option in a favorable matchup against the Chicago Bears.

Etienne to miss time with hamstring injury

New Orleans Saints head coach Kellen Moore announced Monday that RB Travis Etienne Jr. has a hamstring injury that will force him to miss time. He did not reveal a specific timetable.

That leaves the Saints backfield with Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller. I would expect Kamara to handle the bulk of passing downs, while the two likely split ground work.

Kamara has seen nine carries in each game he has played this season and racked up seven targets in those two. The efficiency is gone as he has averaged just 2.6 yards per touch. Still, volume keeps him in play as a potential flex option moving forward.

Miller is an option for those deep league players. He is the more efficient runner of the two, but we know the Saints are not going to just hand him the job over Kamara. He should see enough carries to be in the flex range in deep leagues. How the goal line work is distributed between the two will be huge for fantasy purposes.

Both are volume dependent flex options, with low floors, in a tough matchup against the Falcons next week.

By Eric Karabell

Quarterback J.J. McCarthy, the No. 10 pick in the 2024 NFL draft, is now a member of the New York Giants after they sent a fifth-round pick to the Minnesota Vikings for his services. articles.headline: Oklahoma City says focus is on improving, not the Spurs
articles.description: The Oklahoma City Thunder said they are taking the same approach to the season and are not focused on Spurs after being eliminated by San Antonio in last year's Western Conference Finals.
articles.headlineJa: オクラホマシティはスパーズではなく、自身の成長に集中していると語る
articles.descriptionJa: オクラホマシティ・サンダーは、昨年のウェスタン・カンファレンス決勝でサンアントニオに敗退したものの、今季も同様のアプローチをとっており、スパーズには集中していないと述べた。
articles.body:
OKLAHOMA CITY -- For the Oklahoma City Thunder, the biggest obstacle to another NBA Championship - much less a Finals appearance - resides in San Antonio.

But following a season-ending loss to the Spurs in Game 7 of the Western Conference Finals, Thunder head coach Mark Daigneault said the team's focus entering this coming season isn't solely on whether they can beat the Spurs.

"Our off-season approach, our process is the exact same every single year regardless of if we get eliminated, if we win," Daigneault said Monday during the team's media day. "We take the lessons from the regular season. We really, really dive into the playoff series, but not just the ones that we lose. We audit it. We take the lessons we can. We figure out what we need to add. We figure out what we need to cut.

"The ones where you lose the series are informative, but we don't play San Antonio 82 times, and the most you can play them in a playoff series or in a playoff run, if you're fortunate enough to get to the playoffs, once.

"So we need to make sure that what we are doing is broad enough that it gives us a chance to be competitive across opponents, including ones that we are not aware that are going to be really good teams. That happens every single year."

The Spurs won the regular-season series four games to win against the Thunder last season before the teams faced off in a riveting Western Conference Finals. Thunder center Chet Holmgren struggled against Spurs star center Victor Wembanyama, scoring just eight points in game 1 and just four points on 1-of-2 shooting in the pivotal Game 7.

On Monday, Holmgren reflected on his approach to the offseason as it compared to previous years.

"Yeah, I think I learned a lot from the year that we won it, and I honestly think that my approach was very similar," Holmgren said. "Obviously the emotions of it were different, but I don't think my process changed at all. After we won it, obviously it's good emotions.

"You're at the highest of highs, but at some point -- which was still relatively pretty quick. You have to flush those emotions and look at the reality of what the tape is and then figure out how you can kind of improve on those things. I'd say that was no different after last season. Obviously different emotions, but you still have to get to a baseline where you can look at things objectively and then figure out how to try to improve from there."

The Thunder will return a healthy Jalen Williams, their All-Star guard who played just 33 games last season due to injuries, including a hamstring strain that severely limited him against the Spurs in the playoffs.

"I don't really have too much of like regrets or look back on last year and worry about it," Williams, who was named to the All-NBA Third Team for the 2024-25 NBA season. "It's more how can I avoid doing that last year -- how do I get my body to a point where it won't happen and play and be available for this year."

- Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur have stepped up their interest in Bayer Leverkusen attacking midfielder Ibrahim Maza, TEAMtalk reports. Chelsea, Manchester City, and Aston Villa are also attentively monitoring the 20-year-old, whose versatility and technical quality have made him one of the most highly regarded talents in the Bundesliga.

With Alejandro Balde struggling for game time and considering his future, the Catalan club continue to evaluate targets to reinforce the position and are looking to take advantage of the fact the pair will be free agents.

Discussions to extend the 30-year-old's contract beyond its 2027 expiration have hit a standstill, while recurring injury concerns limited him to just 18 Serie A appearances last season.
